newsitem.title: USA: Edge Petroleum sees Q2 production up.
newsitem.headline: Edge Petroleum sees Q2 production up.

text.p: Edge Petroleum Corp on Monday said it expected second quarter production to be 1.4 billion cubic feet equivalent (Bcfe), a 17 percent increase over the first quarter and a 115 percent increase over the same quarter a year ago.

Edge said it participated in 26 wells for the quarter, all generated in-house, with 20 wells successfully completed, five unsuccessful, and one was awaiting testing, for an 80 percent apparent success rate for the quarter.
Of 20 successful wells, eight were online and producing, and 12 were in various stages of completion and hook-up.
Edge Chief Executive Officer John Calaway said the company expects continued growth rates in the number of wells drilled and production volumes into the third and fourth quarter.
"We expect activity to pick up in the second half of the year," Calaway said. "Our current drilling schedule indicates that we should drill in excess of 100 wells during 1997."

Edge is a Houston-based independent energy company that uses advanced 3-D data visualization and interpretation techniques to explore for natural gas and oil along the onshore Gulf Coast of the United States.
